transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you into the clinic today?
I'm here because... well, after I eat too much, I keep making myself throw up in the bathroom. I do it so I won't gain weight, but it's gotten to the point where I'm scared I can't stop doing it.
Could you tell me your current height and weight?
I'm about five foot six. As for my weight, I'm... I'm really not sure right now. I stopped weighing myself a while back because it just makes me too anxious.
About how much did you weigh the last time you checked?

Honestly, I really don't remember. It's been... well, it's been a long time since I actually looked at a scale. I think I threw mine out over a year ago. So I really couldn't give you an actual number.
Have doctors, family members, or friends expressed concern that you are significantly underweight or too thin?

No, not really. I mean, nobody's ever told me I look too thin or anything like that. If anything, they just don't say much about my weight at all. So, no, no one's been worried about me being underweight.
During these times when you feel you eat too much, do you feel like you can't stop eating or control how much you're eating?

Yeah, that's exactly how it feels. Once I start on those nights, it's like my hands just keep grabbing food even while I'm telling myself, "Lucy, knock it off." I just... I can't stop. I don't feel back in charge until it's already done and everything's gone.
On average, how often each week do these episodes of overeating and making yourself throw up happen?

Well, for at least the past three months, there’s... there's hardly been a week where I didn’t have one of those late-night eating episodes and then go make myself throw up afterward. On average, some weeks it happens several times. It definitely happens more often when I’m stuck at home more because of my back.
